retail.name: Intelligent Retail — Real-Time Customer Analytics
retail.description: Edge-to-core architecture for real-time customer analytics, inventory optimization, and in-store AI experiences. Edge inference on Intel Xeon at each store with centralized model training on Gaudi accelerators.

edge.notes: Low-power E-core for always-on inference — product recognition, demand forecasting, customer sentiment

core.notes: Illustrative P-core tier with AMX; benchmark and size against the selected model and workload

cloud.notes: Train foundation models, generate store-specific model variants

estimated_nodes.small: Illustrative single-site pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.medium: Illustrative multi-site pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.large: Illustrative fleet pattern; sizing and performance validation required

highlights: Edge inference pattern using optimized models on Xeon with Intel AMX
Fleet-management pattern using Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management
Federated learning pipeline — store-level data never leaves the edge, only model gradients aggregate centrally
Event-driven inference can be evaluated where workload behavior and latency requirements allow it

financial_services.name: AI-Powered Fraud Detection and Compliance
financial_services.description: Real-time transaction scoring with multi-model fusion for fraud detection and automated regulatory compliance. Confidential computing via Intel TDX protects sensitive financial data during inference.

edge.notes: Real-time transaction scoring at the branch level, sub-50ms latency requirement

core.notes: Illustrative P-core tier for multi-model workflows; confidential-computing support must be validated for the selected platform

cloud.notes: Train fraud detection models on historical transaction data, backtest against known fraud patterns

estimated_nodes.small: Illustrative single-cluster pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.medium: Illustrative resilient pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.large: Illustrative multi-cluster pattern; sizing and performance validation required

highlights: Multi-model fusion — 3 specialized models (rules, statistical, LLM) vote on each transaction with a judge model synthesizing the verdict
Intel TDX can be evaluated as part of a confidential-computing design where supported
Service mesh and Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security can support a defense-in-depth design
A classification cache can be evaluated for repeated patterns after accuracy and governance review

manufacturing.name: Predictive Maintenance and Quality Inspection
manufacturing.description: Factory-floor AI for predictive equipment maintenance, visual quality inspection, and supply chain optimization. Edge inference on ruggedized Intel hardware with centralized digital twin simulation.

edge.notes: One per production line — vibration analysis, visual inspection, anomaly detection at line speed

core.notes: Digital twin simulation, historical trend analysis, model retraining on plant-specific failure modes

cloud.notes: Train vision models for new product lines, transfer learning across plant locations

estimated_nodes.small: Illustrative single-line pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.medium: Illustrative plant pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.large: Illustrative multi-plant pattern; sizing and performance validation required

highlights: Predictive-maintenance models can use Xeon with Intel AMX after workload-specific validation
OpenShift Virtualization runs legacy SCADA/HMI systems as VMs alongside containerized AI — no forklift migration needed
Tekton pipelines can automate model validation and deployment based on governed quality thresholds
Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management can apply policy across a multi-plant fleet

healthcare.name: Clinical NLP and Medical Imaging AI
healthcare.description: AI-assisted clinical decision support combining NLP for clinical notes with medical imaging analysis. Privacy-preserving inference using Intel TDX for HIPAA-regulated patient data.

edge.notes: Real-time clinical NLP at point of care — classification, entity extraction, summarization in exam rooms

core.notes: Illustrative P-core tier for clinical pipelines; benchmark models and validate privacy controls before use

cloud.notes: Fine-tune clinical LLMs and medical imaging models on de-identified patient datasets

estimated_nodes.small: Illustrative departmental pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.medium: Illustrative hospital pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.large: Illustrative healthcare-system pattern; sizing and compliance validation required

highlights: A staged clinical NLP pipeline can classify, extract entities, summarize, and produce audit events
Intel TDX can be evaluated as one control in a privacy-preserving architecture where supported
Model routing can separate lightweight classification from more complex generation workloads
Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation can support governed storage designs subject to retention requirements

telco.name: 5G Network Intelligence and Edge AI
telco.description: AI-driven network optimization for 5G RAN and core networks. Real-time traffic prediction, anomaly detection, and automated network healing on Intel-powered edge infrastructure.

edge.notes: E-core for power-efficient always-on RAN analytics — traffic prediction, interference detection, energy optimization

core.notes: P-core nodes for UPF, 5G core network functions, and centralized AI model serving

cloud.notes: Train network optimization models on aggregated RAN telemetry, spectrum efficiency models

estimated_nodes.small: Illustrative edge-site pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.medium: Illustrative regional pattern; sizing workshop required
estimated_nodes.large: Illustrative fleet pattern; sizing and performance validation required

highlights: Cell-site inference can be evaluated for RAN optimization after latency testing
Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management can govern a fleet of Single Node OpenShift deployments
Event-driven inference can be evaluated against traffic patterns and response-time requirements
Closed-loop automation requires workload-specific safety, latency, and rollback validation
